name: REC Ltd
title: REC Ltd - 532955 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Analyst / Investor Meet - Outcome

read.thesis: REC targets 10-12% loan growth and INR2.1 lakh crore disbursements in FY27 with H1 loan book up 6% and disbursements of INR90,000 crore, while management concedes NIMs will face pressure from 3.22% levels.

triggers.label: NIM pressure acknowledged
triggers.quote: There will be pressure on my NIMs, but you should take recourse to the fact that we are trying to ensure that our NIMs stay as high as possible.

triggers.label: Competition intense, banks liquid
triggers.quote: we are in a very different phase of competition, where banks are flushed with liquidity and the entire power sector is looking for very low rates.

triggers.label: Loan growth 10-12% FY27
triggers.quote: we are hopeful that we should be able to show around 10% to 12% growth by the end of this year.

triggers.label: Prepayments down to ~INR19,000 crore
triggers.quote: prepayments in the first 2 quarters have come down to only INR19,000 crores.

guidance.value: over INR2 lakh crore, comfortable to achieve INR2.1 lakh crore
guidance.quote: we have set a target of over INR2 lakh crores for our disbursements
We would like to see ourselves touching around somewhere between 10% to 12%.

guidance.value: maintain around 3.0%-3.2%, not going down too much
guidance.quote: our NIMs will not go down further too much
we continuously maintain the 30% dividend payout ratio as mandated by the Government of India.

red_flags.label: NIM compression under competition
red_flags.quote: our net interest margins have come down slightly

red_flags.label: ECL provisioning build-up
red_flags.quote: As of now, we are providing about 1% ECL on our additional loan book.

evasions.quote: sharing specific figures with you may not be possible, because it all depends on promoters
I would not like to hazard and put a figure for the merged entity right now.
We are talking about management control, we are talking about voting rights, we are talking about everything.

summary.headline: REC H1 FY27: disbursements of INR56,457 crore (+67% vs Q1) and net NPA at 0.11%, but management concedes NIM pressure from 3.22% level.
summary.overview: REC reported H1 FY27 with loan book at an all-time high of INR6.17 lakh crore (up 6% YoY) and PAT of INR7,541 crore for the half. Management cited disbursements of about INR90,000 crore in H1 (power sector ~INR80,000 crore), with net credit-impaired assets down to 0.11% from 0.24% a year earlier. Management guided FY27 loan book growth of 10-12% and NIM of about 3.2%, while acknowledging NIM pressure from competition, derisking and rising borrowing costs. The call also covered the pending PFC merger, with the draft scheme awaiting Cabinet approval.

financial_highlights.change: NIM stable per company; management flagged compression
down from INR12,350 crore at 30 June

segments.name: Conventional generation
segments.commentary: Loan book grew about 4% since 31 March 2026; about 11% of Q2 disbursements; thermal is about 24.7% of the book (~INR1.52 lakh crore) per Projects Director.

segments.name: Renewable energy
segments.commentary: RE portfolio at INR86,660 crore as of 30 September 2026, growing ~15% in the half (27% YoY per Chairman); 17% of Q2 disbursements; solar 35%, hybrid 18%, pumped storage 14%, hydro 13%.

segments.name: Distribution / Infra & logistics
segments.commentary: Distribution took 22% of Q2 disbursements; infra and logistics about 10% of the book (~INR62,000 crore), growing ~6% since 31 March 2026.

guidance_outlook: FY27 loan book growth guided at 10-12% (6% achieved in H1).
FY27 disbursement target of over INR2 lakh crore; company expects to reach ~INR2.1 lakh crore, which would exceed last year's INR2.11 lakh crore record only marginally.
NIM expected to hold around 3.2%; management said NIM pressure exists and it would not claim NIM will rise.
Management expects Q3 and Q4 disbursements not to be lower than Q1 and Q2; ~INR70,000 crore of documented projects yet to be disbursed.
Planned sanctions of INR1.7-2 lakh crore in H2; committed pipeline of INR2.56 lakh crore, of which ~INR69,000 crore still to be documented.
Dividend declared for FY27 so far totals INR7.75 per share, including INR3.5 for Q2; 30% payout ratio mandated by GoI.
Stage 1 provisioning around 1% on incremental loan book (ECL); straight 1% provisioning expected to continue.
Merger with PFC: both boards approved; NOC received from RBI and stock exchanges; draft scheme pending Cabinet approval. Management says merged entity will remain government-controlled.
capex_capacity: NEP: minimum ~80 GW additional thermal capacity planned (baseline 215-217 GW to 274-283 GW); ~22-24 GW under construction; REC fund requirement estimated at INR1.8-2.2 lakh crore at INR8.34 crore/MW.
Company targets raising thermal/generation book to ~INR2.5 lakh crore by 2032.
Cabinet approved INR1.85 lakh crore transmission project; detailed guidelines from MNRE still awaited.
NTPC Meja project won: about INR27,000 crore disbursement, half to be shared with PFC.
Rooftop Solar Scheme: ~55 lakh installations achieved against 1 crore target by end of this year; ~95 lakh applications.
demand_pricing: Management attributed FY26 loan growth of only 3% to ~INR1 lakh crore of prepayments despite record INR2.11 lakh crore disbursements; H1 FY27 prepayments were ~INR19,000-20,000 crore.
Competition is intense: banks flush with liquidity, power sector seeking low rates; management said NIM will see pressure.
Management expects yields to hold; loan book is largely floating (about 25%) while about 24% of borrowings are floating, with rising rates seen as favourable.
Thermal yields slightly higher than RE; I&L yields above RE but below thermal; company declined to give specific yield differentials.
Management claims state power utilities borrowed ~INR10 lakh crore in last 3 years, with REC lending INR4.5 lakh crore (~45% share).

qa_highlights.question: What is driving NIM compression and how will the NIM trajectory look?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Kumar said ~24% of borrowings are floating (INR term loans and some ECBs) versus ~25% of the loan book floating, so rate rises are offset; a zero-coupon bond last year gave ~10 bps benefit and the company is seeking withholding-tax exemption on ECBs and a green bond basket mandate.

qa_highlights.question: How will conventional thermal AUM and disbursement grow over the next 2-3 years given slow state capacity additions?
qa_highlights.answer: T.S.C. Bosh cited ~80 GW minimum additional capacity under NEP, implying INR1.8-2.2 lakh crore REC financing needs by 2031-32, with a 30:70 equity-debt assumption.

qa_highlights.question: Will 10-12% growth continue post-merger with PFC in FY28-29?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman declined to give numbers for the merged entity, citing synergies in borrowing, lending and capital base, and restricted guidance to FY27 for REC.

qa_highlights.question: Why is management confident of 10-12% growth given competition from unlisted players and banks?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said prepayments had peaked (INR19,000 crore in H1 FY27 vs ~INR1 lakh crore in FY26), banks face sectoral limits, and power, transmission and biogas (INR23,000 crore scheme) are growth drivers.

qa_highlights.question: Will yields fall further on competitive pricing to state utilities?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Kumar said rebate/concession proposals to state sector are largely settled and yield curve is rising, so limited yield downside is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Is H2 disbursement momentum seasonal or sustainable, and how does the pipeline look?
qa_highlights.answer: Bosh said Q1 weakness reflected documentation delays and peer competition; ~40% of disbursement pipeline is under documentation, and the Chairman cited ~INR70,000 crore of documented projects yet to start disbursement.

qa_highlights.question: How will credit cost evolve now that resolutions are done?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajesh Kumar said ~1% ECL is being provided on incremental loans (~INR300 crore in Q2 on ~INR26,000 crore growth), with ~80% of ECL being reserve-type given state-sector exposure; straight 1% provisioning expected going forward.

risks_watch: NIM compression below 3.2% as competition and rising borrowing costs bite; management admits 'there will be pressure'.
Merger with PFC pending Cabinet approval; government control to be maintained, with final scheme details awaited.
Currency: forex hedging enhanced above INR96/USD; management says no new major forex hit expected but volatility remains.
Smart meter resistance from consumers and perception issues; allocation and completion data not disclosed on call.
Transmission and Green Energy Corridor guidelines from MNRE still awaited; REC's share of INR1.85 lakh crore transmission scheme unclear.
Q3/Q4 disbursement pace versus the INR2 lakh crore-plus target; prepayment trend post rate-hike cycle.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and disbursement pipeline, but candid that NIMs will face pressure from competition and rising borrowing costs. Management was evasive on post-merger targets and on the government-control structure, deferring to pending Cabinet approval.
key_quotes: There will be pressure on my NIMs, but you should take recourse to the fact that we are trying to ensure that our NIMs stay as high as possible.
I am confident that the prepayments scenario has peaked out, and now that we are entering increasing interest rate cycle, I don't think prepayments will be a major issue for us.
We are very confident of touching double-digit growth, and we are hopeful that we should be able to show around 10% to 12% growth by the end of this year.

growth.why: Guides FY27 loan book growth of 10-12% (6% achieved in H1) and disbursements of over INR2 lakh crore (~INR2.1 lakh crore expected), backed by a committed pipeline of INR2.56 lakh crore with ~INR69,000 crore still to be documented; no company-owned capacity additions were given, and NIM is guided only to about 3.0-3.2% amid acknowledged pressure.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: NIM at 3.22% (H1) with spread 2.38%; management flagged pressure from competition and derisking, guiding only to hold around 3.0-3.2%, not an expansion.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No company-owned capacity additions were discussed; REC is a lender, and the ~80 GW thermal build-out is a customer-side financing need, not REC capacity.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Guided FY27 loan book growth of 10-12% versus 6% achieved in H1, and disbursements of over INR2 lakh crore (~INR2.1 lakh crore expected) backed by a committed pipeline of INR2.56 lakh crore with ~INR69,000 crore still to be documented.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed for REC itself; the utilisation read is not applicable to a lender.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 disbursement target is 'over INR2 lakh crore' and expected at ~INR2.1 lakh crore, only marginally above last year's record INR2.11 lakh crore, so there is no sign of a raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: NIM is guided only to around 3.0-3.2% with management conceding pressure, and H1 loan growth of 6% must roughly double to hit 10-12%, so the loan book target is at risk if prepayments or competition persist.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: No new product or model launches were discussed; the biogas scheme and green bond basket are funding or growth items, not launches.

rows.label: PFC merger completion pending Cabinet approval
rows.why: Both boards approved, RBI NOC and exchange NOCs received, and the draft scheme awaits Cabinet approval; management says the merged entity stays government-controlled, but gave no post-merger growth or NIM numbers.

rows.label: NTPC Meja project and transmission financing
rows.why: NTPC Meja win is worth about INR27,000 crore of disbursement, and the INR1.85 lakh crore transmission scheme is Cabinet-approved, though MNRE guidelines are still awaited and REC's share is unclear.

rows.label: Credit quality improvement and provisioning
rows.why: Net credit-impaired assets fell to 0.11% from 0.24% a year earlier and Stage 2 assets dropped to INR3,235 crore from INR12,350 crore at 30 June, with about 1% ECL on incremental loans (~INR300 crore in Q2) continuing.

tone.note: Management was confident on the disbursement pipeline and asset quality but candid that NIM faces pressure from competition and rising borrowing costs, and it was evasive on post-merger targets and government control. Analysts probed the path to 10-12% growth given H1's 6% and the NIM trajectory.
